description: CRIT-206's passThreshold requires: 'A read of whichever artifact/evidence file claims PROP-108a proved confirms a genuinely fresh, real on-chain disbursement transaction hash AND a genuinely fresh, real on-chain repayment transaction hash minted THIS sprint through the real orchestrator functions ... OR the contract explicitly re-defers it ... FAIL if PROP-108a is claimed proved via a fixture, a simulated transfer, or a borrowed artifact.' verification-architecture.md's own Tier-3 section (line 275-283) defines PROP-108a as exactly this: 'a real disbursement transfer (payViaFacilitator), a real repayment transfer, and an independent, separately-performed, finalized-block-confirmed RPC re-verification ... at least one real Base-mainnet-class result,' and explicitly states 'REQ-115/REQ-116's own new orchestrator functions are exactly the code that makes this obligation ATTEMPTABLE for the first time (sprint-1 had no orchestrator to run it through).' Yet state.json's proofObligations entry for this exact artifact anchor (id:PROP-025, tier:3, required:true, artifact:'specs/verification-architecture.md#PROP-108a') is ALREADY marked status:'proved' -- and was marked proved in sprint-1's own Phase 5 (formal hardening) commit 22708f35e, BEFORE the orchestrator existed. Independently read the backing evidence (verification/proof-harnesses/prop-108a-live-mainnet-e2e.mjs + its output.log, file mtimes 2026-07-08 01:48, i.e. sprint-1 Phase 5, hours before sprint-2's own RED/GREEN/refactor commits 71cc1c9/1b1fae2/3151f13 later that day): this harness calls `verifyRepayment` DIRECTLY (never `executeLoanIssuanceAttempt`/`executeRepaymentClaim`, which did not exist yet) against ONE pre-existing, already-mined historical Base-mainnet txHash (0x849362757b4ec7e2a6f982384475a2d08156b2d3162741880e4719ed05598a44) -- there is no disbursement transaction anywhere in this evidence, no payViaFacilitator call, and no involvement of this sprint's own orchestrator functions at all. This is precisely a 'borrowed artifact' by CRIT-206's own definition: a historical on-chain transaction of unknown origin (not shown to be a disbursement THIS system ever made) fed into the read-only verification function to prove the READ path works, misrepresented in state.json as satisfying the full Tier-3 'real disbursement transfer plus a real repayment transfer' obligation. The contract's own text (lines 139-147) explicitly commits to NOT letting this happen ('this contract only commits to NOT silently claiming PROP-108a proved via a fixture, a simulated transfer, or a borrowed artifact') but never actually corrects state.json's pre-existing, still-standing 'proved' marking -- the sprint-2 deliverable leaves this misrepresentation exactly as it found it.

crossCheck.note: Harness imports verifyRepayment directly from lending-verify.mjs (never lending-orchestrator.mjs) and operates on a single, already-existing txHash with no accompanying disbursement transaction or orchestrator call anywhere in the file. Committed in git commit 22708f35e ('Phase 5 formal hardening complete'), which per git log predates all three sprint-2 commits (71cc1c9 RED, 1b1fae2 GREEN, 3151f13 refactor) -- confirming this evidence cannot possibly have exercised REQ-115/REQ-116's own orchestrator functions, which did not exist when it was produced.

resolutionRecommendation: Either (a) re-mark state.json's PROP-025/PROP-108a entry as NOT proved (e.g. status:'deferred' with a note citing CRIT-206's own re-deferral text), matching what the contract's prose already honestly states, or (b) actually attempt the real disbursement-then-repayment pair through executeLoanIssuanceAttempt/executeRepaymentClaim on Base mainnet (or an accepted Base-Sepolia precursor per the Tier-3 policy) and replace the evidence file with one that does so, then update state.json's status/citation to point at that fresh evidence. Leaving state.json as-is (status:proved, citing pre-orchestrator borrowed-tx evidence) is the exact anti-pattern CRIT-206 was written to prevent.
